name: Equity feminism
summary: Equity feminism holds that feminism should seek equal legal and political treatment and equal opportunity for women and men, which it regards as the classical, first-wave goal. It rejects what Christina Hoff Sommers calls gender feminism, with its patriarchy theory, quotas and focus on women as victims, and it welcomes men as fellow citizens. Its economics run from classical-liberal to libertarian.
scope: The classical-liberal strand as defined by Christina Hoff Sommers in Who Stole Feminism? (1994), together with individualist/libertarian feminists such as Wendy McElroy and self-described equity feminists such as Steven Pinker and Camille Paglia, tracing back to the 1848 Declaration of Sentiments. It excludes radical, socialist and gender-focused feminism. Primary texts by Sommers and McElroy could not be opened, so positions rest on secondary descriptions and most non-gender answers are low-confidence inferences from its classical-liberal and libertarian lean.

keyFigures.name: Christina Hoff Sommers
keyFigures.role: Philosopher who popularised the equity versus gender feminism distinction in Who Stole Feminism? (1994)

keyFigures.name: Wendy McElroy
keyFigures.role: Individualist feminist listed as an equity feminist and editor of Freedom, Feminism, and the State

keyFigures.name: Camille Paglia
keyFigures.role: Writer who describes herself as an equity feminist favouring equality before the law

universal-healthcare.rationale: Equity feminism has no healthcare doctrine; its libertarian strand (McElroy) distrusts state provision while its mainstream liberal strand is relaxed, so adherents split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Equity feminism asks only for fair pay and equal treatment (s1), and its market-friendly individualist strand (s6) leans against state wage-setting; inferred, not stated.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Individualist feminists describe themselves as pro-market and credit capitalism with widening women's options (s6), though Sommers-style equity feminists rarely make it a central claim.

public-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal and libertarian leanings of the strand; no source ties equity feminism to nationalisation, and individualist feminists oppose state expansion.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not an equity-feminist issue; the market-friendly individualist wing would resist higher taxes, so this is an inference from that lean.

unions-good.rationale: Equity feminism takes no line on unions; the libertarian wing is wary of them while a liberal wing welcomes them, so adherents are split.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments complains that married women lost all right in property (s5), and individualist feminists treat property rights as protecting women; strength of the commitment is inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Equity feminists want employers to hire on skill and pay fairly (s1) but the individualist strand prefers less intervention in private economics (s6); inferred lean.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Sommers-aligned conservative equity feminists would lean yes and liberal ones no, so adherents split.

worker-ownership.rationale: No source supports worker ownership as an equity-feminist aim; the strand's market and property emphasis suggests it is not a goal.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the libertarian and civil-liberties side of the strand; the sources do not discuss surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Individualist feminists oppose state interference in adults' choices about their own bodies (s6), from which drug legalisation is inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Sommers criticises gender-feminist campus speech codes and sensitivity campaigns (s2), and the individualist strand opposes state restriction of expression; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Equity feminism rests on equal legal rights and limits on state power; a leader bypassing institutions runs against that, though sources never address it.

state-harmful.rationale: Individualist feminists see government as a historic oppressor of women (s6), but mainstream equity feminists rely on the state to guarantee equal legal rights, so the radical claim is rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: The sources are silent; libertarian-leaning adherents oppose limits and liberal ones accept them, so this is split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; no strand position follows from equal-treatment principles, and adherents range from libertarian to conservative.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Individualist feminists argue that banning sex work to protect women treats women as a monolith and removes their choices (s6); Sommers-style equity feminists are less committed, so medium.

decide-locally.rationale: No source speaks to centralisation; equal rights are usually sought through national law, but the libertarian wing favours decentralisation.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed by any source on the strand; adherents range across criminal-justice views.

traditional-family.rationale: Sommers is described as defending traditional marriage and femininity against feminist critique (s7), while individualist feminists oppose enforced roles (s6); adherents split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from equal treatment under law and individualist freedom of association; sources do not cover it and conservative adherents may dissent.

abortion-legal.rationale: Individualist and libertarian feminists support reproductive rights including abortion and call themselves pro-choice (s6); Sommers-aligned conservatives are less uniform, hence medium.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments objects to women's subordinate place in church as well as state (s5); the strand is not hostile to faith but does not seek a larger public role for it.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Equity feminism rejects quotas and special preferences (s4) but holds that law must secure equal rights for all, so active correction is contested among adherents.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Sommers faults gender feminism for refusing to recognise differences in temperament and desires (s4, s7); equity feminists hold gender differences are not wholly social.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not an equity-feminist topic; adherents range from cosmopolitan libertarians to cultural conservatives.

gradual-change.rationale: Equity feminism works through reform of law, within existing institutions (s1), but the sources do not take a stand on social change generally.

reduce-immigration.rationale: No source addresses immigration; libertarian adherents lean against restriction and conservative ones for it.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from the strand's distrust of state power and its focus on national legal equality; sources are silent.

free-trade.rationale: Individualist feminists credit capitalism with raising women's living standards (s6), from which support for free trade is inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents split between libertarian cosmopolitans and conservatives.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Nothing in the sources bears on it; the strand includes both non-interventionist libertarians and hawkish conservatives.

open-borders.rationale: The libertarian wing may favour open borders but the Sommers/AEI mainstream does not; inferred and split, so a mild no.

limit-growth.rationale: The strand's market optimism suggests rejection of growth limits; sources do not discuss environment.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No equity-feminist position exists, and adherents range from libertarian skeptics of state action to liberals.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed by any source; no strand position follows from equal-rights principles.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nothing in the sources bears on nuclear power; adherents split by wider politics.

revolution-justified.rationale: Equity feminism seeks equal treatment through law and existing institutions (s1) and rejects the radical transformation of society sought by gender feminists (s3); inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Sommers attacks academic feminist experts for advocacy-driven research and fabricated statistics (s2, s3), implying distrust of expert authority as such; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: The strand's market and individualist emphasis (s6) rules out central planning; the sources do not discuss it directly.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; market-friendly adherents would accept markets with any ownership, but would not endorse the restriction.

land-value-tax.rationale: Equity feminism is a doctrine about sex equality in law and opportunity, and neither Sommers nor McElroy discusses land taxation, so the position is left neutral.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from property emphasis and the pro-market lean; the sources do not discuss inheritance.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; libertarian adherents are split on it and liberal adherents lean yes.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from the strand's pro-market lean (s6); sources do not mention tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from the strand's preference for limited state economic intervention (s6).

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the strand supports property rights but takes no stand on its distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred from the strand's market and property emphasis; it has no anti-wage-labour tradition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Only libertarian adherents hold this; mainstream equity feminists never address it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages conflict with individualist feminism's opposition to engineering equality through state economic control (s6); inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Equity feminism rests on equal legal rights and political participation (s1, s5); one-party rule is contrary to that, though never discussed.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments invokes the republican Declaration of Independence against male rule (s5), but modern equity feminism takes no position on constitutional monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments demands the franchise as an inalienable right (s5); modern equity feminism assumes liberal democracy, though never states a view on bad votes.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed by sources; no position follows from equal rights.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred from the strand's liberal-democratic and individualist commitments; no source discusses councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Libertarian adherents accept secession; mainstream equity feminists never address it.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments rejects the claim that men are by nature fit to rule women, and its principle of equality extends against natural-rulers claims generally (s5).

political-violence-never.rationale: The sources do not address it; liberal equity feminism would condemn it but self-defence and resistance rights make adherents split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from liberal individualism; nothing in the sources addresses war.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Declaration objects to women's subordination in church and state alike (s5); Sommers-style conservatives are mixed on strict separation, so a mild inferred yes.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Equity feminism demands equal legal rights and the Declaration of Sentiments attacks church-backed female subordination (s5); scripture-based law is incompatible.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Only libertarian adherents accept this; mainstream equity feminists never address it.

military-superiority.rationale: No source speaks to it; adherents range from libertarian to conservative.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Equal rights regardless of birth is the core of the Declaration of Sentiments (s5); an ethnic nation is an inference from that universalism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Equity feminism rejects the Marxist-tinged victim analysis Sommers ascribes to gender feminism (s3, s2), which includes class-conflict reasoning; inferred from that rejection.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Equity feminism seeks equal opportunity and equal treatment, not equal results (s1), and Sommers condemns quotas as gender-feminist (s4).

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: None of the sources on equity feminism discuss indigenous land claims, and nothing in equal legal treatment settles them either way.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; the strand's individualism and distrust of group-based claims (s6) suggest rejection.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from individualist and liberal commitments; sources silent.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Individualist feminism builds on self-ownership and individual autonomy (s6), but the sources do not argue for self-interest as a moral good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Individualist feminists hold that rights belong to individuals and oppose treating persons as representatives of a group or collective (s6).

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy lies outside what the sources attribute to equity feminism, so adherents can hold either view.

limit-population.rationale: The strand opposes state interference in reproduction (s6), from which rejection of active limits is inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The pro-capitalist wing credits industrial economies with improving women's lives (s6); sources do not discuss the claim directly.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The sources say nothing about the pace of technological change, and nothing in equal-opportunity principles favours or opposes it.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from the individualist principle that adults control their own bodies (s6).

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from the strand's emphasis on individual autonomy and limited state; no source covers it.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the libertarian side of the strand; sources are silent.

restore-past-order.rationale: Equity feminism is rooted in progress toward legal equality since Seneca Falls (s5, s2), so it does not treat restoring a lost order as paramount, though Sommers-type conservatives value tradition.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Sommers demands honest evidence over ideological claims (s2), but the statement is a general stance the sources do not tie to equity feminism.

direct-action.rationale: Equity feminism works via law and institutions (s1); direct action is inferred as disfavoured.

means-match-ends.rationale: Equity feminism works through ordinary law and reform, but the sources do not take up the prefigurative claim that methods must mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred from the strand's pro-modernity, pro-market lean; no source touches it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Equity feminists favour choice rather than abolition, and Sommers defends women's freedom to choose family-centred lives (s4, s7), though the Wikipedia article cites a radical agenda of abolishing the gender-specific division of labour only as Schenk's view, not equity feminism's (s1).

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred from the property and market emphasis of the strand; sources do not discuss it.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from the strand's market lean; sources do not discuss it.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Equity feminism rejects the Marxist-influenced victim framework of gender feminism (s3, s2); profit-as-exploitation is a Marxist claim, so this is inferred from that rejection.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Contrary to equal legal rights for all, which is the core of the tradition (s5); never discussed.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred from the strand's property and individualist stance.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred from the pro-capitalist lean of the individualist wing (s6); not discussed.

taxation-theft.rationale: Libertarian feminists would agree, but mainstream equity feminists would not; adherents split.

harm-principle.rationale: Individualist feminists oppose government interference in adults' choices about their own bodies (s6), which matches the harm principle; no source cites it by name.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individualist feminists call treating people as simply representatives of their sex collectivist (s6), and equity feminism centres equal individual rights (s1).

conscription.rationale: Equal treatment would require women's inclusion if it existed (ERA tradition, s1), but individualist feminists oppose compulsion; sources do not directly address it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The tradition demanded the vote (s5) but no source weighs the freedom to leave a country against it, so this is left neutral.

state-as-business.rationale: No source treats governments as firms; individualist feminists distrust the state but equity feminists still rely on it for legal equality.

positive-liberty.rationale: Individualist feminists oppose government engineering of equality in private economics (s6); freedom is negative liberty plus equal law, though Sommers speaks of the freedom to pursue happiness (s4).

media-academia-power.rationale: Sommers argues gender feminists control women's studies programmes and academic institutions, but the claim that universities and media outweigh elected officials is an inference, not stated.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Race and ability sit outside the sources on equity feminism, and adherents do not share a view; Sommers stresses evidence but takes no side here.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred from individualist and liberal democratic commitments; no source discusses corporatist representation.

total-state.rationale: Individualist feminists see government as a historic oppressor of women and oppose state engineering of social life (s6).

national-rebirth.rationale: Equity feminism seeks incremental legal and cultural equality, not national renewal; this is an inference from its reformist liberalism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Foreign expansion is never discussed in the sources; the inference is only from the strand's liberal, individual-rights outlook.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Contrary to the equal-rights, republican basis of the Declaration of Sentiments (s5); never discussed.

bound-labor.rationale: Equity feminism descends from abolitionist-linked individualist feminism that opposed bondage and demanded rights to wages and property (s5, s6).

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Sommers attacks the gender-feminist redefinition of knowledge and the curriculum transformation movement (s2, s3), defending evidence over standpoint claims.

universal-morality.rationale: Individualist feminism draws on natural-law arguments for equal rights of men and women (s6), though the sources do not discuss moral truths in general.

single-common-good.rationale: Inferred from individualism and distrust of collectivist claims (s6).

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The sources on equity feminism do not touch Zionism, and adherents' views follow their wider politics rather than the strand.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora citizenship rules are not addressed by any source on equity feminism, so no position can be derived.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is unrelated to anything the sources attribute to equity feminism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the property emphasis of the strand; not addressed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from the libertarian and conservative lean of Sommers' AEI milieu and the strand's choice emphasis; sources do not discuss schooling policy.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not part of equity feminism; libertarian adherents lean towards balanced budgets and others do not, so it is split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Individualist feminists link women's freedom to economic freedom and capitalism (s6); mainstream equity feminists do not state it.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred from the legal-equality and rule-of-law basis of the tradition; not discussed.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-determination of nations is absent from the sources, and adherents' opinions follow their general liberal or conservative leanings.

force-without-un.rationale: Military doctrine is unaddressed by the sources; adherents range from non-interventionist libertarians to hawkish conservatives.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Sommers insists on evidence over feeling in feminist claims (s2) but the strand includes religious women, so the sweeping statement is not endorsed.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Immigrant welfare eligibility is never discussed in the sources on equity feminism, so no position is derived.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Conservative adherents agree, liberal ones do not; the sources are silent.

class-collaboration.rationale: Equity feminism asks employers to provide equal opportunity and hire on merit (s1), a cooperative rather than class-conflict picture; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred from the strand's classical-liberal character; sources do not discuss it.

dominated-front.rationale: A bloc against Western powers is foreign to a Western, liberal-democratic feminism; this is inferred from its outlook, not stated.

workers-nation.rationale: National versus international labour organisation is unrelated to equity feminism; the lean is inferred from its individualism over class or nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The tradition began by condemning laws that kept women subordinate in public life (s5), and individualist feminists say legally enforced gender roles harm both sexes (s6); equity feminism demands the state treat the sexes equally (s1).

ban-interest.rationale: A legal ban on lending at interest conflicts with the strand's contract and market emphasis (s6), though no source discusses it.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Equal rights before the law regardless of group is the core of the tradition, which grew out of abolitionism (s5, s6); no source discusses segregation directly.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Equity feminism rejects the Marxist-influenced analysis Sommers assigns to gender feminism (s3, s2), which includes the view of the state as an instrument of domination.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not discussed by the sources; adherents' views follow wider politics.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The sources do not take up immigrant assimilation, and adherents divide between libertarian and cultural-conservative positions.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no basis in the sources; rejected by inference.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not addressed in the sources on equity feminism.

national-mission.rationale: A mission to spread one's government abroad is not discussed; the inference is from the strand's liberal individualism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Sommers rejects the claim that American society is a patriarchy keeping women cowering and submissive, regarding it as a gender-feminist notion (s3, s7), and equity feminism holds that legal equality has largely been achieved (s2).

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The sources do not address it; mild populism is possible among libertarian adherents, but the claim is not part of the strand.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Individualist feminists oppose state interference in reproduction and in adults' choices about their bodies (s6).

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Legal accountability for state killings is not discussed by any source on equity feminism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Libertarian feminists agree, but equity feminism overall relies on the state for equal legal rights and many adherents accept a larger state; split.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equal individual rights regardless of group is central to the tradition (s5, s6), and individualist feminists opposed marriage laws (s6).

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments asserts that all men and women are created equal with inalienable rights (s5), and equity feminism's core demand is equal treatment of women and men by the state (s1).

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-internal question that equity feminism does not address.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Whether settler states are colonial projects is not discussed by the sources and does not follow from equal treatment of the sexes.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal treatment under one law is the core of equity feminism (s1), though no source discusses religious personal-status law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from individualist freedom and the tradition's objection to church subordination (s5).

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred from individualist opposition to state restrictions on private conduct (s6).

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between secular liberals and religious conservatives.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine contrary to the strand's liberal commitments; not discussed.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments adopts the principle that governments derive just powers from the consent of the governed and applies it to women (s5).

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the pro-free-trade lean; sources do not discuss mercantilism.

population-transfer.rationale: Contrary to equal rights for every individual, the tradition's core (s5, s6).

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian feminists (McElroy) would agree, but mainstream equity feminists accept state coercion for law enforcement; split.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; market-friendly adherents might agree but the framing is Social Darwinist.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred from the strand's free-speech and civil-liberties side; not discussed.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments objects to men's absolute tyranny over women (s5) which echoes the idea, but the strand does not state a republican theory of freedom.

separated-powers.rationale: Equity feminism seeks equal rights through law and courts under constitutional government (s1, s5); checks and balances is inferred rather than stated.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined revolutionary vanguard is a Leninist idea alien to a movement seeking equal rights through law (s1); inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The sources never rank the poor's needs above others; adherents range from market-minded to liberal and the claim is left neutral.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; the property-owning lean suggests sympathy but sources are silent.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is not addressed in the sources; libertarian adherents distrust state labour rules and liberals differ.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; liberal individualism leans against the claim.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Equity feminism rests on equal rights for individuals regardless of group (s5); the claim is not discussed, and conservative adherents may dissent.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's demand to vote and hold elective office in ordinary democratic terms (s5).

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from the strand's legal-equality and civil-liberties commitments.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price caps conflict with the pro-market lean (s6) though no source discusses them; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Sommers' critique centres on honest information and freedom of inquiry (s2, s3); government control of media is contrary to the strand's liberal outlook.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party command of the army contradicts the liberal constitutionalism of the tradition (s5); this is inferred, not discussed.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not addressed by the sources, and adherents are split.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; inferred lean from a pragmatic liberal outlook.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding party discipline sits poorly with individualism (s6); no source discusses it, so low confidence.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between libertarian skeptics and liberals.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from preference for constitutional limits.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the strand takes no stand on church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments condemns women's subordination in church and state (s5), and equity feminism demands equal legal rights, incompatible with clerical political rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist position unrelated to the strand; inferred rejection.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Individualist feminists oppose state interference in adults' choices (s6); Sommers attacks campus moral policing (s3).

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential terms are not discussed; the mild no is inferred from the limited-government outlook of the individualist wing (s6).

recall-officials.rationale: Recall elections are not addressed by any source on equity feminism.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is unaddressed; libertarian adherents agree and conservatives disagree, so it is split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Forbidding rent conflicts with the contract and property emphasis of the strand (s6); no source discusses housing.

people-in-arms.rationale: Armed citizenry versus a professional army is not addressed; libertarian and liberal adherents differ.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The moral value of rural versus urban life is not addressed in any source on equity feminism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification of divided nations is outside what the sources attribute to equity feminism.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Sommers criticises academic feminists as detached from ordinary women's views (s3) but the claim about the educated generally is not hers.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Equity feminism upholds universal equal rights across cultures (s5); a relativist stance is inferred as disfavoured, but sources do not discuss it.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not discussed in sources on equity feminism, and adherents divide along wider political lines.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents split between libertarian parental-choice and liberal views.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Sommers invokes evidence and science against ideological claims (s2); inferred rejection, though the sources do not discuss it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Individualist feminists oppose government regulation of adults' choices (s6) and contrasted themselves with feminists seeking anti-pornography laws; Sommers is less explicit, so medium.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship law is not addressed; the mild no is inferred from the strand's universalist equal-rights principle (s5).

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy for minorities is not addressed by the sources, so no position follows.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; equal-law principle opposes exemptions while liberty favours them.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Individualist feminists criticise gender roles that limit autonomy (s6); the explicit Millian claim is inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Cancelling debts cuts against the contract and property emphasis (s6); inferred, as the sources never discuss it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Whether political independence requires economic transformation is a postcolonial question the sources do not cover.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-writing procedure is not addressed in the sources.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Trading freedoms for growth contradicts the liberal, rights-first outlook of the tradition (s5); inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is not discussed; libertarian adherents reject aid duties and liberal ones accept them.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear strategy is not addressed in any source on equity feminism.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The method of electing a head of state is not addressed in the sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank design is not addressed by the sources on equity feminism.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial compromise in conflicts is not discussed by the sources.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Individualist feminists treat property rights as individual protections (s6), so conditioning them on the common good is disfavoured.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The nature of the Soviet Union is a dispute internal to Marxism and unrelated to equity feminism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Sommers' critique of alarmist, poorly evidenced claims (s2) suggests scepticism of acting before evidence; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance commitments like NATO's Article 5 are not discussed in the sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The legal status of annexed territory is not addressed by the sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Declaration objects to church-backed subordination (s5) but equity feminists do not seek curbs on churches' property.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources never touch constitutional design of the head of state, and nothing in equal-rights principles settles it.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Military responses to secession are not discussed in any source on equity feminism.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy arrangements such as one country, two systems are not addressed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contrary to the republican equal-rights founding of the tradition (s5); not discussed.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; market-friendly adherents lean yes but the question is not a feminist one.

character-from-environment.rationale: Sommers faults gender feminism for denying innate differences in temperament and desires (s4); equity feminists accept both nature and nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments indicts rulers' unaccountable power as tyranny (s5), and equity feminism is a demand for equal legal treatment (s1).

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not addressed by the sources and does not follow from equal-rights principles.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not discussed in the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Public cults of a national leader conflict with the equal-citizen liberal individualism of the tradition (s5); inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Equity feminists push for equally shared household responsibilities (s1) and equal treatment of sexes in law; the specific equal-time presumption is inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This Maoist thesis belongs to an internal Marxist debate and is unrelated to equity feminism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Seizing estates cuts against the property-rights emphasis of the strand (s6); sources do not discuss land reform.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not addressed by the sources, so no position follows.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims to territory on grounds of nationality contradict the individual-rights universalism of the tradition (s5); inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Equal individual rights and liberty of conscience are core to the tradition, which criticised church subordination of women (s5).

women-must-cover.rationale: A law forcing women's dress is the kind of sex-specific legal burden equity feminism opposes; individualist feminists oppose state interference in adults' choices about their bodies (s6) and the tradition demands equal legal treatment (s1).

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not discussed in the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic political unity is an inference-only no from the strand's individualism over group identity (s6).

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is not addressed in the sources.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The tradition fought for equal rights within existing states (s5); the minority-emigration question is not discussed.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Equity feminism rejects the Marxist-tinged analysis of gender feminism (s3); inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is not discussed in the sources on equity feminism; market-friendly adherents might accept it or not.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are unaddressed; libertarian adherents say no and others are split, so it is neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Equity feminism relies on courts and constitutional amendments (ERA) to secure rights against majorities (s1); inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Sommers contrasts equity feminism with gender feminism's emphasis on quotas (s4), and equity feminism seeks equality of opportunity rather than imposed outcomes (s1).

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: An autarkic bloc contradicts the pro-trade, pro-market lean of the individualist wing (s6); the sources do not discuss it.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Linking trade deals to labour and environmental standards is not addressed in the sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material incentives with moral ones contradicts the market and individual-choice emphasis (s6); inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foco-style revolution is far from the legal-reform method of equity feminism (s1); inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments denounces rule by status and inherited authority over women (s5); abolition of hereditary titles is an extension of equal legal rights.

history-own-civilization.rationale: History curriculum framing is not discussed, though Sommers criticises ideological curricula (s3).

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule by a more advanced society contradicts the tradition's universal claim of equal rights (s5); inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Patriotic education is not addressed in the sources, and adherents divide between liberal and conservative views.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Equity feminism rejects quotas and preferences as gender-feminist special pleading (s4); by extension of the same equal-treatment principle racial preferences are opposed, though sources do not discuss race.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is outside the sources; the mild no is inferred from the market lean.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The pro-capitalist wing credits capitalism with improving women's lives (s6); inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating influence in former imperial regions is unrelated to anything in the sources.

delink-world-market.rationale: The strand's pro-market, free-trade lean (s6) is opposed to economic delinking; sources never address development theory.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Marxist thesis about imperialism, rejected by inference from equity feminism's opposition to Marxist-influenced frameworks (s3).

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equity feminism asks employers to hire on skills not names or backgrounds (s1) but libertarian strands (s6) defend freedom of association, so adherents lean against with some dissent.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Equal Rights Amendment tradition sought entrenched constitutional guarantees of equal rights (s1).

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The validity of colonial-era treaties is not addressed by the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments claims the elective franchise as a right (s5); inferred to extend to choosing rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Giving every dissenter a veto is a Calhounian or anarchist principle with no support in the sources on equity feminism.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments follows the Declaration of Independence in justifying resistance to a ruler who abuses rights (s5); adapted by inference.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty versus monarchy is not discussed in the sources.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not addressed in the sources on equity feminism.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use for food and research is not addressed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: A duty of the privileged is not part of any source on equity feminism, and individualist and conservative adherents differ.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The tradition is built on women claiming a place in public life (s5); inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Sommers rejects the gender-feminist claim that culture and media reproduce a domination structure (s3).

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim from the Marxist tradition that equity feminism rejects along with gender feminism's framework (s3); inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is a Marxist-influenced claim that equity feminism does not share; inferred from its market lean (s6).

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for the native-born contradicts equal individual rights (s5); inferred, not discussed.

party-own-road.rationale: This question concerns relations among communist parties and is unrelated to equity feminism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not addressed in the sources on equity feminism.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Demands for territory lost in past wars are not discussed in the sources.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Group-based political privilege conflicts with equal rights before the law (s5); inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional anti-fascism is not addressed by the sources, and adherents' opinions follow their general politics.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The equivalence thesis is not discussed; the mild yes is inferred from the strand's liberal, anti-collectivist outlook.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The tradition grew out of abolitionism (s5, s6), so downplaying slavery's role is unlikely; no source discusses the war's causes.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is not discussed by the sources, and adherents are divided.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: In The War Against Boys, one of her two defining books, Sommers argues forcefully that boys are on the weak side of the education gap and are neglected by policy; equal concern for both sexes is the strand's stated aim.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Sommers disputes inflated claims about male violence against women (s7, s3) and equity feminism seeks fairness for both sexes; the exact symmetry claim is inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The tradition holds equal rights are universal (s5); inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political guardian role for the military contradicts the liberal constitutionalism of the tradition; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Individualist feminists oppose government engineering of private economic life and family arrangements (s6), and equity feminists respect unpaid family choices without seeking to pay them as labour (s4).

filial-duty.rationale: Sommers defends traditional family values (s7) but individualist strands do not endorse legal duties; split.

office-by-exam.rationale: Examination-based civil service is not discussed, though merit-based hiring is in the spirit of equity feminism (s1).

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Blocking foreign purchases conflicts with the pro-market and property emphasis (s6); the sources do not discuss it.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Declaration complains that divorce laws were framed against women (s5), and individualist feminists oppose state control of marriage (s6); Sommers' alleged blame of feminists for divorce rates (s7) makes the strand mixed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandates and instant recall are not discussed in the sources on equity feminism.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed; libertarian adherents favour private accounts and others do not, so it is neutral.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land held only while used conflicts with the property emphasis (s6); the sources do not discuss it.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Representative consent is basic to the tradition's constitutionalism (s5); inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Official-language policy is not addressed in the sources.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Bans on foreign owners conflict with the property-rights emphasis (s6); inferred, not discussed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Equity feminism holds equality means equal treatment and opportunity, not equal outcomes, and Sommers criticises quotas (s1, s4); treating unequal outcomes as discrimination is the gender-feminist view.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism is not discussed in the sources, and adherents' views follow wider politics.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert support for foreign insurgents is not addressed in the sources.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: A great power invading an ally to keep it in a bloc contradicts the liberal outlook of the tradition; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign money are not discussed in the sources; market-friendly adherents lean against the worry and others share it.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Restrictions on foreign NGO funding conflict with the civil-liberties side of the strand; inferred, not discussed.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Individualist feminists oppose state engineering of family and reproductive choices (s6).

residents-only-property.rationale: Local residency limits on property purchases conflict with the property-rights emphasis (s6); inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state job guarantee conflicts with the pro-market lean (s6) and is not discussed in the sources.

democratic-peace.rationale: The democratic peace thesis is not addressed in the sources on equity feminism.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Libertarian adherents deny a general duty to obey while mainstream equity feminists, who rely on law for equal rights, accept one; split.

non-intervention.rationale: Absolute non-intervention is not addressed, and adherents range from isolationists to interventionists.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed in the sources on equity feminism.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred rejection of conspiracy claims; Sommers demands evidence (s2).

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Individualist feminists have argued for marriage without state licence (s6) but mainstream equity feminists support legal marriage; split.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom-of-information rights are not discussed in the sources.

local-production.rationale: Buying local conflicts with the free-trade lean of the individualist wing (s6); inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Affinity-group organising is an anarchist doctrine; equity feminism works through law and institutions (s1), so a mild no is inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The primacy of national versus international law is not addressed in the sources.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining a nation by religion contradicts the universal equal rights of the tradition (s5); inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Ritual tribute to a leading power contradicts the equality and liberal outlook of the tradition; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Interregional fiscal transfers are not discussed in the sources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The strand defends private property generally (s6); inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold War strategy is not discussed in the sources, though Sommers opposes Marxist-tinged feminism (s3).

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The mild yes is inferred from the market-friendly lean (s6); service delivery is not discussed in the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: Sources do not treat religion as an illusion, and the strand includes religious adherents, so a mild no is inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Cato-aligned wing credits capitalism with better lives for women (s6); inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Equity feminism seeks equality through equal legal treatment and opportunity without challenging the existing economic order (s1), which is the position the statement denies.

socialized-care.rationale: Individualist feminists opposed state involvement in childcare (s6), and equity feminism leaves household arrangements to families (s1).

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is unrelated to equity feminism; the mild no is inferred from individualist liberalism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaty rights of nations within states are not discussed in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Commune-style society is not discussed, and the strand's property emphasis suggests it is not a goal.

majority-settlement.rationale: Encouraging the majority to settle minority regions contradicts equal rights for individuals (s5); inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The pro-capitalist wing credits capitalism with improving women's lives (s6), so a third way is not sought; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Competing historical land claims are not addressed in the sources.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Sommers insists on evidence-based claims (s2); the statement is a factual falsehood and is rejected by inference.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Individualist feminists oppose state interference in adults' private choices (s6).

suppress-opposition.rationale: The tradition claims political voice for the excluded (s5); suppression of opposition is opposed.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Individualist feminists oppose state interference in adults' expression and conscience (s6), and the tradition criticised church-dominated law (s5).

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Governing colonies for the ruling country's benefit contradicts equal-rights universalism (s5); inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is an Islamist doctrine of religious duty not addressed in sources on equity feminism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's opposition to religiously justified subordination (s5).

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct participation in workplaces and universities is not discussed by the sources.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Sommers criticises gender feminism's victimhood analysis and ideological framework (s3, s2), of which intersectional oppression theory is a descendant; the specific term is not discussed in the sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; equal protection suggests yes but Sommers-aligned adherents are split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Libertarian adherents lean yes; conservatives no; the sources are silent.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The left-right dichotomy is not discussed in the sources, and adherents place themselves variously.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation is a Marxist concept, and equity feminism rejects Marxist-influenced frameworks (s3); inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Universal equal rights principle (s5) argues against essentialising a religion, though critics of Islamic gender law exist in the strand; inferred, contested.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments grounds authority in the consent of the governed (s5), not in God-given male rule.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules in state institutions are not addressed by the sources.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; libertarians dislike regulating contracts while equity feminism supports equal workplace treatment (s1).

social-market-economy.rationale: The ordoliberal model is not discussed in the sources on equity feminism, and adherents split between more and less regulation.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Total disarmament is not discussed; the mild no is inferred from the strand's mainstream liberalism, which accepts state defence.

rich-first.rationale: Unequal development sequencing is not addressed in the sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Alignment between great-power blocs is not addressed by the sources.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession contradicts the republican equal-rights founding of the tradition (s5); inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist banking is not a doctrine of equity feminism and conflicts with the strand's market lean; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF conditions are not addressed in the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments claims the vote as an inalienable right rather than a privilege of property (s5).

domination-women-nature.rationale: Sommers attacks gender feminism's patriarchy-based theories (s3), of which ecofeminist domination claims are an instance; inferred.

reification.rationale: Reification is a Marxist-Lukacsian concept outside equity feminism, whose sources do not discuss it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A Marxist argument that equity feminism rejects along with gender feminism's framework (s3); inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Equity feminism asks that the state treat the sexes equally under law (s1), which presupposes general standing laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments claims the vote as an inalienable right against exclusion by group, and the tradition grew from abolitionism (s5, s6).

online-participation.rationale: Online deliberation is not discussed in the sources on equity feminism.

open-government-data.rationale: Open government data is not addressed by the sources.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Individualist feminists opposed state control of marriage (s6), and equal rights is the tradition's core (s5).

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting shops by owners' religion contradicts equal treatment regardless of group (s5); inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are not addressed in the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not addressed; adherents include religious conservatives and secular liberals.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The pro-capitalist wing does not share the worry (s6); inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Equal treatment by the state is the core principle (s1); inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Individualist feminists oppose state imposition of beliefs (s6).

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Libertarian anarchists may dissent, but mainstream equity feminism relies on law enforcement of equal rights; inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational government is not addressed by the sources on equity feminism.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Libertarian and conservative adherents lean yes; not addressed in sources.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources, and adherents differ.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not addressed in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential risk is not discussed in any source on equity feminism.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments objects that women are excluded from ministry and kept subordinate in church (s5); equity feminism does not seek to force churches, hence medium.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Declaration of Sentiments condemns laws making wives civilly dead and subject to husbands' authority (s5), and equity feminism calls for equally shared household responsibilities (s1).

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Franchise for foreign residents is not addressed, though the tradition cared about the franchise for excluded groups (s5).

rent-control.rationale: Rent caps conflict with the market and property emphasis (s6); inferred, not discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Libertarian feminists differ among themselves on patents and copyrights, and no source covers it.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled youth movements contradict liberal individualism; inferred, not discussed.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Basing nuclear weapons is not discussed in the sources.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign military bases are not addressed by the sources.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Official recognition of past genocides is not discussed in the sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Equity feminism defends property and ownership income, so a mild no is inferred (s6).

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Strict pacifism is not part of equity feminism, though no source discusses self-defence; mild no inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: National historiography is not addressed by the sources.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Sommers faults gender feminism for refusing to recognise innate differences (s4); equity feminism treats sex as biological, and Pinker, an equity feminist, holds that the doctrine makes no claim against biology (s1).

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Equity feminism defends equal treatment of women as a group under law (s1), against post-structural scepticism; sources do not discuss it, hence low.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring national martyrs is not discussed; the mild no is inferred from liberal secular individualism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: A spiritual framing of politics contradicts the secular legal-equality outlook of the strand; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The role of a homeland for a diaspora is not addressed.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cultural renewal versus state-building is not discussed in the sources.

god-not-male.rationale: Religious language is not addressed, and adherents include religious conservatives and secular liberals.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The strand does not judge scripture by feminist standards; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Reserving economic life for the majority contradicts equal rights regardless of group (s5); inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative merging of regions for one people is not addressed in the sources.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence from the state is not discussed; the mild yes is inferred from the strand's civil-society, anti-state lean (s6).

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: What counts as socialism is a Marxist-internal dispute unrelated to equity feminism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public ownership of local utilities conflicts with the pro-market lean (s6); inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Bicameralism is not discussed in the sources.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal ownership of production conflicts with private property emphasis (s6); inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Libertarian-municipalist confederalism is not discussed in the sources.

family-wage.rationale: Equity feminism asks that pay be fair and equal for equal work (s1, s2) and rejects the sex-specific assumption of a male breadwinner (s5).

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Faster regulatory approval fits the libertarian side of the strand (s6) but no source discusses medical regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anti-ageing research funding is not addressed in the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Untraceable payments fit the libertarian side of the strand (s6); not discussed in the sources.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online pseudonymity is not addressed in the sources on equity feminism.

person-over-state.rationale: Individualist feminists treat each person as an end and oppose treating people as representatives of a group or tools of the state (s6).

spiritual-nature.rationale: The spiritual dimension of politics is not addressed in the sources.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Whether regional powers can be withdrawn is not addressed.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural biotechnology is not addressed in the sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban density and the environment are not discussed in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Individualist feminists criticise treating people as representatives of a group as collectivist (s6), and equal individual rights is core.

racial-pride.rationale: Racial pride is not addressed by the sources; equity feminism's individual-rights focus leaves it neutral.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Use-of-force doctrine is not addressed in the sources.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Linguistic definitions of nationhood are not discussed in the sources.

communal-electorates.rationale: Group-based voting conflicts with equal individual franchise (s5); inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: A claim that foreign powers plot partition is a conspiracy-type claim with no support in the sources; inferred rejection.

free-public-college.rationale: Tuition-free public college conflicts with the pro-market lean (s6); the sources do not discuss education finance.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is not addressed in the sources on equity feminism.

future-generations.rationale: Intergenerational environmental duty is not addressed in the sources.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Sommers' freedom feminism respects women's own distinctive choices (s4) but equity feminism does not hold that women bring different political values that deserve extra weight (s1).

arms-reduction.rationale: Arms control is not addressed in the sources.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Secret versus open treaties is not discussed in the sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital controls conflict with the pro-market, free-trade lean (s6); inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: A state monopoly on arms is not discussed; libertarian adherents dissent and others accept it, so it is split.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Mass refusal of orders is not part of equity feminism; the mild no is inferred from its law-and-institutions orientation (s1).

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wage-setting by bargaining is not addressed in the sources, and adherents differ.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Wage top-ups are not discussed in the sources on equity feminism.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Legal fiscal rules are not addressed in the sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Reshaping international economic rules for poor countries is contrary to the free-trade lean (s6); inferred, not discussed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Equity feminism works through reforms in law and the ERA-style amendment (s1); abolishing the state is rejected.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Experimentation with economic systems is not addressed in the sources.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural capital accounting is not addressed in the sources.

sacred-nation.rationale: A sacred national community is contrary to liberal individualism (s6); inferred rejection, not discussed.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Debt cancellation conflicts with the contract and property emphasis (s6); inferred, not discussed.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Internal colonialism comes from Marxist-influenced theory, which equity feminism does not share (s3); inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Sommers holds that men and women share equal status but differ in temperament, a position that presupposes a stable human nature (s4); the statement's claim about redesign is not discussed.

public-service-media.rationale: Public broadcasting is not addressed in the sources on equity feminism.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Perennialism is not addressed in the sources.

farm-price-support.rationale: Guaranteed crop prices conflict with the pro-market lean (s6); inferred, not discussed.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear disarmament policy is not discussed in the sources.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from its classical-liberal framing of equal citizenship regardless of group; the sources do not discuss class parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from equal legal protection for girls and women; individualist feminism would treat cutting of non-consenting girls as a harm the law should prevent, but the sources do not address it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equity feminism traces to the 1848 Declaration of Sentiments, which protested women's lack of property rights, and demands equal legal treatment of the sexes.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no feminist or liberal principle settles the question.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the libertarian strand of equity feminism's preference for property rights and courts over agencies; adherents range from classical liberal to libertarian.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from its demand for identical legal treatment of the sexes and individual equality before the law, which sits poorly with customary authorities.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from its classical-liberal and libertarian lean, which resists overriding individual liberty; not discussed in the sources.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from classical-liberal scepticism of fixed state penalties; the sources do not discuss sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents' classical-liberal views could go either way.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from equity feminism's classical-liberal and libertarian economics, which favour voluntary association over compelled dues.

voter-id.rationale: Equity feminism has no stated position on ID at the polls; liberal and libertarian adherents are not united on it.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its classical-liberal equal-treatment principle, which implies the state should not privilege one religious interpretation.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from its classical-liberal lean toward limited, rule-based government; sources do not discuss the definition of democracy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Equity feminists defend women's free choices and reject enforced gender roles, so they accept women's sex outside marriage, but it is not a central or forceful theme and Sommers is socially moderate.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its individualist and libertarian opposition to state restriction of liberty.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: classical-liberal and libertarian thought (Friedman) favours a negative income tax over welfare bureaucracy, but the sources do not state it.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1848 Declaration of Sentiments, the founding text of this tradition, protests that women are denied the franchise, and equal political treatment is the core equity-feminist demand.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Equity feminism, as the Declaration also condemns church limits on women (s5), but Sommers-style equity feminists do not make religion a main cause; adherents split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Equity feminism concerns sex, not race; Pinker-type adherents accept some biology of differences while others accept the construct view, so it is split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: equity feminism seeks equal legal treatment and rejects quotas and gender-parity machinery, and its libertarian strand opposes extra state bodies.

missingStatements.text: The law should treat women and men identically, with no sex-specific protections or burdens.
missingStatements.rationale: Equity feminism is defined as demanding equal state treatment of the sexes (s1) and Camille Paglia opposes special protections for women.

missingStatements.text: Most differences in pay and career outcomes between men and women reflect differences in choices rather than discrimination.
missingStatements.rationale: Sommers faults gender feminism for ignoring differences in temperament and desires as explanations of pay differentials and has denied the gender pay gap (s4, s7).

notes: Equity feminism is partly defined against gender feminism by its own proponents, and the split is contested by other feminists. Libertarian and conservative adherents differ on economics, abortion, and the family, so many such answers are low confidence or neutral.
